Maybe either find a new profession or start working on something else. This is too long to work on the same project,’” she said.
Then, in 2019, Stockett was dropped by her publisher Penguin, and she went from being a literary Cinderella story back to being almost as unmoored as when she started.
But she “refused to give up.” In fact, she said the firing was “liberating.”

“There’s something scrappy inside of me. I think part of that has to do with coming from Mississippi. If you kick me, I’m going to come back stronger and kick back harder. I think that’s what I did,” she said.
It was only when Stockett moved back to Mississippi that she could start on the more “honest” version of the story, she said, and it “started to blossom.”

The move came in tandem with a breakthrough in the research process. Stockett learned about sterilization laws across the U.S. that prevented people from having children and according to Stockett was a means to “cleanse society of these so-called ‘undesirables.’”
“It shocked me so much that I thought, ‘I got to write about the women who endured that,’” she said. “And the women who had that threat looming over them.”

The resulting book, “The Calamity Club,” is an uproarious, action-packed, 656-page book about two outcast women and their quest to find a girl who ends up in an orphanage. The book also weaves in the topics that Stockett was afraid to broach after “The Help.”
“If you want to write an honest story in Mississippi about women, you have to include hypocrisy, racism, sexism and all the absurdities that come along with it,” she said.

title: What Tim Curry Shared About His Mysterious Love Life
summary: Was Tim Curry ever married? Here’s what he shared about his love life and sexuality in his memoir.
story: As fans remember the legacy of iconic actor Tim Curry, much of his love life remains a mystery. And according to what the “Rocky Horror Picture Show” star has said in the past, that’s how he wants it to stay.

Tim Curry, who passed away “peacefully at his home” at the age of 80 on Aug. 25, has said little about his romances over the course of his storied career. In his 2025 memoir “Vagabond,” Curry gives readers just a tiny glimpse into that world — and nothing more.

“I guarantee you, if it matters, that I have experienced true love, true heartbreak, and everything in between, including no small amount of wreckage. Which, naturally, helps inform who I am,” the famously private Curry wrote in his book’s introduction.  “I have loved and been loved and I hope you have, too.”
He added that he is “not interested in your romances.”
“And specifics about my affairs of the heart or the bedroom are—respectfully—none of your f—--- business,” Curry wrote.

The actor is known for his roles in the 1985 comedy “Clue,” 1990 miniseries “It” and 1992 Christmas flick “Home Alone 2: Lost in New York.” However, he is best recognized for his portrayal of hypersexual mad scientist Dr. Frank-N-Furter in the 1975 musical film “Rocky Horror Picture Show.” And while Frank, whom Curry also portrayed in the stage production of the musical, is incredibly open with his relationships and desires, the actor wrote in his memoir that he wasn’t much like him — to many a fan’s chagrin.

“People often expected me to be brash or aggressive, like Frank. That’s still what is most desired from me when I meet strangers. I know I’ve disappointed audiences because I’m much quieter and more reserved,” Curry wrote. “If I actually existed on Frank’s level in my everyday life, I would have burnt out long ago.”

Privately, however, Curry said he did exercise the freedom that Frank-N-Furter espoused. In a 2025 interview with the New Yorker, he mentioned that the character empowered him to “decide not to limit myself to anything.”

“It gave me a lot of oomph — a lot of strength — to back up my own decisions about my life. And I certainly didn’t limit myself sexually, particularly. I thought that was important at the time,” he told the outlet. “I swam ‘the warm waters of sins of the flesh,’ to quote the play and the movie.”
He reiterated, however, that ultimately his “romantic life is none of anybody’s business.”

Despite his commitment to keeping his love life private, he was openly crazy about one particular gal: Miss Piggy. Curry, who also starred in the 1996 film “Muppet Treasure Island,” described the lovable ham as “quite a seductive girl.”

“She’s always funny, and never boring. Although I did say at the outset that I wouldn’t speak about any of my romantic relationships, I will say that Miss Piggy and I had quite a good time together, both on set and in our trailers,” Curry wrote in his memoir.”
And luckily, Curry wrote, that he was able to keep his fling with the fabulous Muppet on the DL.
“Fortunately, our dalliances never led to any tension with Kermit— I was clever about it,” he wrote in the book.

title: Who Was Dolly Parton’s Husband, Carl Dean? Everything She Said About Their 60-Year Marriage
summary: Here’s what Dolly Parton said about her husband Carl Thomas Dean before she died. Here’s a story about their marriage.
story: Dolly Parton and her husband, Carl Thomas Dean, were married for nearly 60 years, and died within a year and a half of each other.
While the country music legend had been in the spotlight since the ‘50s, her relationship with the businessman mostly remained out of the limelight.

Parton, a star on the stage, television and film, died on Aug. 25, 2026, at the age of 80. Her nephew Bryan Seaver confirmed her passing in a video message shared on her Instagram page. He did not mention a cause of death.
The news of her death came about a year after Parton had to postpone multiple concerts as a she faced “health challenges.”
Her death also followed the loss of her beloved husband, who died on March 3, 2025, at the age of 82.
She penned a sweet statement at the time reflecting on their decades of marriage.

“Carl and I spent many wonderful years together. Words can’t do justice to the love we shared for over 60 years. Thank you for your prayers and sympathy,” she wrote on her Instagram, alongside the announcement of his death.
Dean, who was from Nashville, was a businessman without any industry ties. In a 2023 interview for “What Would Dolly Do? Radio,” the singer gave insight into her long-standing private relationship.
“Carl has never been in the limelight and all, never wanted to be in it. He don’t like it,” said Parton.
She shared that after one public outing, he knew that life wasn’t for him.

“He went to one thing with me early on when we first married to a BMI Song of the Year (event), and he came out there taking off his tuxedo, his tie and all that and said, ‘Don’t ever ask me to go to another one of these damn things because I ain’t going,’” she said. “I never asked him and he never did.”
The couple also never had children, though in a 1984 interview with Andy Warhol in Interview Magazine said they tried to “for years.”

Parton spoke about how independence in her marriage led to a thriving career, telling Oprah in 2020, “Since I had no kids, and my husband was pretty independent, I had freedom. I think a big part of my whole success is the fact that I was free to work.
But despite their different approaches to public life, the two had a lasting relationship, celebrating 58 years of marriage before his death.
Here’s a look back at the major events in their relationship, from their first meeting at a laundromat to his support for her music.
Parton and Dean Met in 1964

Many people can live in a city for years before going on a date, but Parton met her husband on her very first day in Nashville. She told the New York Times that she brought a lot of dirty clothes with her, and stopped at the “Wishy-Washy” laundromat.

“After I’d put my clothes in the machine, I started walkin’ down the street, just looking at my new home, and this guy hollered at me, and I waved,” Parton told the New York Times in 1976. “Bein’ from the country, I spoke to everybody. And he came over and, well, it was Carl, my husband.”
In that 1976 interview, Parton had more to say about their first meeting.

“I wouldn’t go out with him. I mean, that was somethin’ we was taught. You gotta know somebody or they may take you on a back road and kill you. But I said, ‘You’re welcome to come up to the house tomorrow because I’m baby‐sittin’ my little nephew.’”
She said he came over every day for a week, and they sat on the porch and talked. “I wouldn’t even take him in the house,” she said.
But the first day she didn’t have to babysit, she said that Dean took her to meet his parents. “Cause he said he knew right the minute he saw me that that’s the one he wanted.”
They Had a Secret 1966 Wedding

After dating for about two years, Dean proposed to her and they wed in May of that same year. While preparing for her wedding, the upcoming nuptials caused tension between her and her then-manager, Fred Foster.
“He asked me not to get married. He said it’ll make it so much harder if you’re married with all this promotion,” she said in a 2012 interview with Chattanooga, Tennessee, NBC affiliate WRCB.
“My mother-in-law had already sent out invitations,” Parton said. “It broke her heart because I said we had to call the wedding off.”

But that didn’t stop the two from getting married in a more private ceremony the following weekend. Only her mother, Avia Lee Owens, and Pastor Don Duvall and his wife were present at Ringgold Baptist Church where they tied the knot.
Parton Wrote ‘Jolene’ in 1973

One of her most famous songs, “Jolene” tells the story of a woman begging for Jolene not to “take her man.” Parton said this was inspired by a “flirtation” that her husband had with a woman working at the local bank.

“She got this terrible crush on my husband,” Parton told NPR in 2008. “And he just loved going to the bank because she paid him so much attention. It was kinda like a running joke between us — when I was saying, ‘Hell, you’re spending a lot of time at the bank. I don’t believe we’ve got that kind of money.’ So it’s really an innocent song all around, but sounds like a dreadful one.”
Parton Got Close with Her Bandleader in the 1980s

In a 1986 interview with Ladies’ Home Journal, republished in her book, “Dolly on Dolly: Interviews and Encounters with Dolly Parton,” the country icon spoke about how she had gotten “wrapped up” in an “affair of the heart” in 1982.

She told the outlet she’d faced the disloyalty of “a special friend, an affair of the heart, which just about killed me. Oh, I cried an ocean. But I ain’t gonna talk about it anymore,” she said, playfully. “I’ve got to keep some mystery.”
Parton said at the time that she and Dean were not divorcing, reiterating what she has said years earlier.

“We’ll just always be together,” she told People in 1982. “To him it’s all a joke. There ain’t a man in this world could ever live up to my husband. That’s one of the things that keeps me from going too far.”

In a 1982 interview with Barbara Walters, Parton confirmed that she’d been stuck at home in Tennessee for health issues alongside her husband. She joked that her months at home had “just about busted” their relationship.
“I’m glad to be going,” she explained. “He’s glad for me to be going and so we’re glad to get back to our abnormal.”
In the Walters interview, Parton added that she and her husband were “flirts” but were faithful “best I know how.”

“I just love people there and ... being a woman away from home, there are these good looking guys that come on to you pretty strong. And every now and then I like to come on pretty strong myself,” she said. “But I know that I’ve got something at home, that I wouldn’t threaten or take a chance on losing for anything in the world.”
Parton Said She and Dean Were Still a Team in 1997

In a 1997 interview with Out Magazine in which she promoted her latest collection of dance club remixes, Parton explained that she and her longtime companion, Judy Ogle, was “just an old maid” and not her lover.

“People think because she’s never married that she must be a lesbian, and because we’ve been together, that we must be lovers. But the fact is, I think Judy would rather be called a lesbian than an old maid,” she quipped. “If I was gay, I’d certainly never find a finer person than Judy as a mate. I’m as close to her just about as I am with (my) husband.”
She also responded to rumors about her husband being out of the picture.
“They don’t ... see my husband because he hates being in the limelight. But I see him all the time,” she told the outlet.
Parton added that the secret to her decadeslong marriage was simple.
“We just make a point to enjoy the stuff we enjoy and stay out of each other’s faces. I don’t get in his s---, and he don’t get in mine. And we get along great.”

The Out interview, along with many others, were reported in the 2017 book “Not Dumb and Not Blonde: Dolly in Conversation.” The book — which cites Parton and Randy Schmidt as authors — collected and published interviews with Parton dating as far back as 1967.
Parton and Dean Renewed Their Vows in 2016
In May 2016, Parton and Dean got the wedding they planned years ago, but never got to have. The private affair was held at their Nashville-area home, and she said they “just had fun with it.”
“I got all dressed up in the most beautiful gown you’ve ever seen and dressed that husband of mine up. He looked like a handsome dude out of Hollywood,” Parton told Rolling Stone.

“We had a few family and friends around. We didn’t plan anything big at all because we didn’t want any kind of strain, any kind of tension, any kind of commotion, so we planned it cleverly and carefully. We just had a simple little ceremony at our chapel at our place. We just had just a few people who needed to be there to make sure they got the pictures and the few things that we needed.”
Parton also said that their vow renewal inspired a large portion of her album “Plain and Simple,” which was released that August.
Parton Surprised Dean with a Playboy Look for His Birthday in 2021
In honor of her husband’s birthday, Parton donned a throwback look that she knew he would love. In July 2021, she put on a Playboy bunny costume in his honor.

“Remember sometime back I said I was going to pose on the cover of Playboy Magazine when I was 75? Well, I’m 75 and they don’t have a magazine anymore,” she said in a video at the time. “But my husband always loved the original cover of ‘Playboy’ so I was trying to think of something to do to make him happy.”

Parton was the first country star to pose for the now-defunct magazine, appearing on the cover in 1978. According to her official website, her contract at the time had “very specific parameters that did not include nudity,” but she still wore the classic bunny suit.
In her 2021 video, she said that she had a new cover made with her fresh outfit and “the new Dolly.”
“Well, the old new Dolly,” she said, good-naturedly. “In the first one, I was kind of a little butterball in that one. Well, I’m string cheese now.”
“But he’ll probably think I’m cream cheese,” Parton said with a wink. “I hope!”
Parton Released Her 2023 Rock Album with Dean’s Support
The singer released her “Rockstar” album in 2023. On “What Would Dolly Do? Radio,” she spoke more about her husband’s reaction to hearing the album.

“I played him the whole album and he said, which to me was the greatest compliment in the world, he said, ‘You know, it’s pretty good,’” she said. “That would be like anybody else saying, ‘Oh, that’s best I ever heard. That’s just so fantastic.’”
She said Dean has always been honest with her about his opinions.

“I had done a couple of things in the past, just some rock things. He said, ‘It’s OK. It’s OK,’” Parton added. “He’s very honest. We have such a great relationship. I know not to ask him if I don’t want an honest answer.”
Parton Announced Dean’s Death in 2025
On March 3, 2025, a statement was shared on Parton’s Instagram announcing the death of her husband.

“Carl Dean, husband of Dolly Parton, passed away March 3rd in Nashville at the age of 82. He will be laid to rest in a private ceremony with immediate family attending. He was survived by his siblings Sandra and Donnie,” the statement read, followed by a personal message by Parton.
“Carl and I spent many wonderful years together. Words can’t do justice to the love we shared for over 60 years,” the singer wrote. “Thank you for your prayers and sympathy.”

title: More Than 130,000 People Want To Rename Nashville International Airport After Dolly Parton
summary: Fans, fellow musicians and more are hoping to rename the Nashville International Airport in Tennessee after the beloved Queen of Country.
story: Fans, fellow musicians and more are hoping to rename the Nashville International Airport in Tennessee after the beloved Queen of Country.

A Change.org petition advocating for the renaming of the airport to the “Dolly Parton International Airport,” has drawn more than 130,000 signatures as of Aug. 27. While the petition was started nearly two years ago, it has skyrocketed in support in the days since the country icon’s death on Aug. 25, with big names like fellow country singer Sheryl Crow backing the effort.

“Since her passing, tens of thousands of additional supporters have visited and signed this petition,” Tennessee locals Lydia Popovich and Dan Dion, who launched the petition, wrote in an  update to the petition on Aug. 25. “The outpouring of support has reinvigorated our mission — to rename the Nashville International Airport to Dolly Parton International Airport.”
They added that “Dolly deserves to be remembered and celebrated.”
“What a wonderful way to share her light and magic across Tennessee and the world,” the two wrote on the petition’s page.

Parton died “peacefully” at her home in Nashville on Aug. 25 after a brief battle with cancer, according to a statement from her estate. She was 80 years old. Hours after her death, interest in the petition, which was launched in January 2025, surged.

The page was flooded with comments from fans along with many others who have benefited from Parton’s many philanthropic efforts that ranged from her Imagination Library, which has donated hundreds of thousands of free books to children, to the My People Fund, which has helped victims of wildfires and natural disasters.

“Dolly’s Foundation is the only entity that gave financial support to my son (as well as everyone who lost their home) in the 2016 Gatlinburg fire,” one supporter wrote on the petition. “With that money he was able to have a down payment on another house.”
Another supporter wrote about Parton’s contributions to child literacy.

“The most important humanitarian ambassador in history for child literacy and various charity efforts deserves this honor,” the supporter wrote of the name change. “On top of her selfless lifestyle, she was one of the most brilliant musicians to ever live. America mourns Dolly Parton.”
The momentum has made an impact. Nashville Metro Councilmember Russ Bradford said on Aug. 26 that he is sponsoring a resolution to signal the council’s support for the change.
In a response to the petition, Bradford wrote of Parton that “few people have done more to define what this city means to the rest of the world.”

“Renaming BNA in her honor would be a fitting tribute to someone whose generosity and hometown pride have never wavered,” he wrote in the response, posted to the petition’s page. BNA, the airport’s code, is derived from its original name Berry Field, an ode to World War I veteran Harry S. Berry.

The petition has also received support from State Rep. Todd Warner, a Republican lawmaker who previously sponsored a bill to rename the airport to honor President Donald Trump. Warner withdrew that bill following pushback, but has indicated he would support the renaming of BNA as a tribute to Parton.
“It will be one of the first bills that I file if someone doesn’t beat me to it in November,” Warner told local outlet WKRN.

While the petition has gotten support from legislators, the final decision comes down to the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority, which said it is aware of the request. Currently, a 2010 policy doesn’t allow for the renaming of the airport after a figure until two years after the individual’s death, an airport authority board member told Axios. The airport itself however has already paid tribute to the star, lighting up in pink in honor of her legacy.

“Dolly Parton was not only a singer and songwriter but also a philanthropist and entrepreneur. Above all, she was a Tennessee legend who made significant contributions to our state and communities,” the airport wrote on Instagram. “From tonight through the weekend, our parking garages will be illuminated in pink to honor Dolly and her lasting impact in Tennessee and around the world.”

title: Andy Cohen and Boyfriend Kevin Sobieski Just Took a Big Step in Their Romance
summary: Andy Cohen and his new boyfriend Kevin Sobieski are officially making it public.
story: Andy Cohen and his new boyfriend are officially making it public.

The “Watch What Happens Live” host and businessman Kevin Sobieski stepped out at a public event for the first time when they made an appearance at friend John Mayer’s live SiriusXM performance on Aug. 26 in the Hamptons in New York.
Their big night out came more than two months after Cohen first shared that he was dating someone new.
The longtime Bravo producer spoke in June on his SiriusXM podcast about how he has “met the person.” Cohen, 58, did not reveal Sobieski’s name at the time, but he gushed about his new relationship.
“This man is kind, and strong, and smart, and he is an adult,” Cohen said on his podcast. “And he loves my children, and they love him, and I love him.”
Pop culture expert Nessa Diab appeared on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle on June 4 and shared some details of the new summer romance, including Sobieski’s name.
“We’re happy for him,” Jenna and Sheinelle replied.
Cohen said on his show that the two met at a July 4 party in 2025.

“We talked all night: I very methodically put my number in his phone,” Cohen said. “Apparently, I said to him twice that night, ‘I want to make sure this number is right … and then he said, ‘Wow, I knew you were serious when you were really, like, serious about this number.’”
Cohen also introduced Sobieski to his children, Benjamin Allen and Lucy Eve.

“We have been so slow and deliberate and methodical about getting to know each other, and introducing him to the kids, and just entering him into the equation of my family so slowly,” Cohen said. “It has been so easy. One year later, I still can’t believe I found him.”
One area where Cohen has had to educate Sobieski is the “Real Housewives” universe. Cohen said on TODAY on Aug. 5 that his boyfriend has never seen a single episode of Bravo’s hit reality franchise.
“His algorithm is feeding him ‘Housewives’-related things because our phones listen to everything we say. So he’s starting to, I think, get a sense of the universe. But he has no clue,” Cohen said.
Cohen is not bothered by it.
“No, not at all. I love it. He loves my kids and me, and that’s what’s important,” Cohen said. “But I’ll get him there.”

title: Which ‘Married at First Sight’ Season 20 Couples Are Still Together Now?
summary: Which couples are still together from Married at First Sight Season 20? Here’s what happened at the reunion.
story: The first Peacock-produced season of “Married at First Sight” ended on Aug. 27, wrapping up the fates of seven couples arranged by two experts.

By the time the finale rolled around, two couples had already called it quits. Five more weighed in on whether they’d continue with their relationship. The reunion provided even more of an update on all the couples.
Here’s what happened in the finale and the reunion.
Devin Short and Caitlin Grimm
Status: Not together
Devin and Caitlin ended their relationship five days before Decision Day amid fights during a couples retreat. This was preceded by tension over their communication style.
One of the last things that Caitlin said about Devin was that while he was a “fantastic” human, they were “clearly not compatible.” Caitlin also revealed she has a boyfriend.
Nick Unlenhuth and Courteney Landis
Status: Not together
Nick and Courteney broke up in front of all the other couples following prodding from hosts Paul C. Brunson and Dr. Liza Paz at a group therapy session.
Both agreed the relationship wasn’t working. The couple had experienced tension and a lack of intimacy since their wedding day.
After an emotional reunion and a spar with Adam, Courteney revealed she had a boyfriend, who was also in the audience.
Felipe Cruz and Tori Dahl
Status: Not together

Felipe and Tori broke up after Felipe shared thoughts that distressed his bride. Off-camera, he confessed that he had been thinking of being unfaithful with her constantly. Felipe, during the reunion, corroborated having these thoughts, but said he’d never cheated.
The breakup wasn’t too surprising, considering Felipe struggled with the idea of monogamy throughout the process. He continually expressed becoming bored once in a relationship.
Mecca Amen and BelléJolie Force
Status: Not together
BellèJolie and Mecca hit plenty of road bumps during the process, with BellèJolie often feeling like she liked Mecca more than he was able to reciprocate.
In the finale, though, both chose to stay married. Mecca burst out smiling when BellèJolie chose to marry him. “For me a yes means continuing to show up and doing it better,” he said.
However, the reunion provided another update: BelléJolie revealed that they had quickly split up after Decision Day.
Nikki Jefferson and Shawn Best
Status: Not together
Nikki chose to break up with Shawn on Decision Day, saying that she didn’t feel emotionally safe with Shawn. As typical between Nikki and Shawn, the conversation became defensive.
Marissa Meyer and Adam Dehmlow
Status: Not together

Marissa began Decision Day by saying that she had fallen in love with Adam. Ultimately, though, she chose not to marry him. She felt like she was changing her personality to please him, repeating a pattern that she had in past relationships.
At the reunion, Marissa and Adam’s showdown was enough for Caitlin to call it a “dumpster fire.” Marissa revealed Adam had messaged Tori on Hinge; he said he wasn’t trying to pursue her.

Adam revealed that he has a girlfriend. The camera panned to her in the crowd, who was shocked by the revelation and stayed silent. When asked her thoughts on Adam after hearing everyone’s commentary during the reunion, she said her experience with Adam didn’t match up to what others were saying.
Cameron Mitchell and Michelle Le
Relationship status: Still married
Cameron and Michelle are the only couple from “Married at First Sight” still together. At the reunion, the two shared they are happily married and that Cameron proposed again.

Michelle also shared a health update at the reunion. Diagnosed with uterine fibroids at 26, Michelle said her case worsened. She said she ultimately got a hysterectomy. The couple is now living together in the Bay Area.

title: Dolly Parton’s Siblings: What to Know About Her 11 Brothers and Sisters
summary: Dolly Parton, who died on Aug. 25, was one of 12 siblings. Her death was announced by her sister Cassie’s son Bryan Seaver. Here’s what to know about Dolly Parton’s siblings.
story: Dolly Parton’s large, tight-knit family was always her backbone as she became a country music icon.
The deep bond with her siblings, nieces, nephews and others has been in the spotlight since the 10-time Grammy winning singer-songwriter died “peacefully” on Aug. 25 in Nashville, Tennessee.
Her death was announced by family in a video message from her nephew Bryan Seaver, the son of Dolly Parton’s sister Cassie Parton.
Her younger sister, Stella Parton, also shared a remembrance of Dolly on Facebook on Aug. 27.

“My sister was one of the most generous, thoughtful and kind people I’ve ever known,” she wrote. “What the world saw is exactly who she was, so much so, she told me recently that if there was no hope for her, she would still allow her medical team to try experimental drugs in the hope of helping others in the future.”
Dolly Parton was one of 12 children. Raised by Robert and Avie Lee Parton, the kids grew up in the Appalachia region of rural Tennessee, according to the Country Music Hall of Fame.

Music was a common bond they shared over the years, helping them to work through difficult times when the family was struggling to get by. Several of her siblings performed with her on various specials and variety shows over the years.
In the first of more than 50 appearances on TODAY, Parton shared the importance of her family with former co-anchor Jane Pauley in a 1978 interview.
“I’m extremely close to my family, and my nieces and nephews are extremely close to me,” Parton said.
She said that several of her younger siblings had lived with her at times.

“I know what it feels like to know that responsibility, but it would be a while before I would want children, if I ever do,” she said. “I don’t think I would miss having ‘em because I’ll always have lots of kinfolks around me.”
One of her nieces, Jada Star, spoke about Parton’s closeness to her siblings and relatives in an appearance by the Parton family on The Hallmark Channel in 2016.
“I just remember you always being so present and loving us so much,” she told Parton. “All the kids. We were all your kids.”
“That’s true,” Dolly Parton said. “You still are.”

When another one of her nieces, Hannah Denison, survived a childhood leukemia diagnosis, Dolly Parton made a large donation to Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville where Denison was treated. She also wrote the song “Chemo Hero” as a tribute to Dennis and a fundraiser for the hospital.

Dolly Parton has six living brothers and sisters: Willadeene, Robert Jr., Stella, Cassie, Freida and Rachel. Five of her brothers have died: Larry, in 1955 when he was just a baby; Floyd, in 2018 at age 61; Randy, in 2021 at age 67; David, in 2024 at age 82; and Coy, in July 2026 at age 82, per People.
Read on for everything you need to know about Dolly Parton’s 11 siblings.
Willadeene Parton

Willadeene Parton, born March 24, 1940, is the eldest of Dolly Parton’s siblings. She “tends to act as a second mother to her younger siblings,” according to a post on Dolly Parton’s official website.

Willadeene Parton, now 86, pursued a career as an author. In 1996, she published a memoir about the Parton clan titled “Smoky Mountain Memories: Stories from the Hearts of the Parton Family.” The following year, she released “All-Day Singing & Dinner on the Ground,” a compilation of recipes from the Parton family.
David Parton

David Parton, who worked as a bridge builder superintendent, died Nov. 15, 2024, at age 82 at his home in White Pine, Tennessee, sister Stella Parton announced. A cause of death has not been revealed.
Sharing news of her brother’s death, Stella Parton posted on Threads, saying that her brother “finally got his angel wings. RIP dear soul. Love you forever.”
Before his death, David Parton largely lived his life out of the spotlight, though he had been photographed escorting Dolly Parton to events, according to Woman’s World.
Stella Parton

Stella Parton, an acclaimed musician born May 4, 1949, was 11 when she made her recording debut with sisters Dolly and Cassie Parton, singing on their uncle Bill Owens’ album, per the Smoky Mountain DNA website, which traces Dolly Parton’s family origins.
Since then, Stella Parton has released more than 30 albums, starting with “I Want to Hold You (In My Dreams Tonight),” which came out in 1975.

Stella Parton, now 77, released a memoir in 2011 titled “Tell It Sister, Tell It: Memories, Music and Miracles.” She has explored acting, too, with appearances in the film “Dolly Parton’s Coat of Many Colors” (2015) and “Dolly Parton’s Christmas of Many Colors: Circle of Love” (2016).
While promoting the 2022 Pure Flix original movie “Nothing is Impossible,” Stella Parton revealed to People that she considers herself a “loner in (her) family.”
“Everybody knows that I’m independent,” she said. “But if they need me, if they call me out to help with something, producing, consulting or whatever, I’m always there.”
Stella opened up about life with Dolly in an appearance on actor and comedian Vicki Lawrence’s talk show “Vicki!” in the early 1990s.
“We would write songs together, and she always wrote the good lines and would laugh at my bad ones,” Stella said.

“The main thing I didn’t like was she loved to tell dirty jokes, and they used to sit in the back of the school bus, and she’d always make me sit in front of the bus because she said I was too young to hear the jokes they were telling in the back, and that would always just drive me crazy,” she added.
Stella also shared a remembrance of Dolly on Facebook Aug. 27 in the wake of her death.

“My big sister Dolly got her wings this past Tuesday,” she wrote. “If anyone gets to heaven I’m sure she made it right on time. I know she’s showing out big time, in all her sparkles and shine. That was my sister’s way.”
Stella remembered talking with Dolly on the phone every Tuesday before the sun came up.
“We would catch up on gossip, as sisters do, and drink coffee and make plans as it has always been our way,” she wrote.
Stella also paid loving tribute to Dolly’s qualities.

“My sister was one of the most generous, thoughtful and kind people I’ve ever known,” she wrote. “What the world saw is exactly who she was, so much so, she told me recently that if there was no hope for her, she would still allow her medical team to try experimental drugs in the hope of helping others in the future.
“My sister was always thinking of others and if you want to honor her legacy, show more kindness, lift others up and give more of your time and resources as she continued to do to the very end.”
She also remembered Dolly’s sunny disposition.

“Dolly loved the world and everyone in it,” she wrote. “I would criticize and complain about it and she would laugh and say; ‘shoot Tedda, we’ve got more important things to do than worry about their silly asses.’ She was right and she proved it everyday.
“She left the world a better place by being in it so let’s  follow her example.”
Cassie Parton
Cassie Parton, born on Feb. 12, 1951, first recorded music at age 10, singing backup vocals with sisters Dolly and Stella Parton, the Smoky Mountain DNA project revealed.
In 1970, she sang with her sisters on “The Porter Wagoner Show,” and she performed as a vocalist in the 2013 Dollywood production “My People: Dolly’s Letter Home,” according to Knox News.
She also appeared in an episode of the TV series “Dolly” and had a role in the 2022 film “Dolly Parton’s Mountain Magic Christmas,” according to IMDb. Nowadays, she leads a fairly private life.
Her son Bryan Seaver served as Dolly Parton’s head of security for two decades.
Randy Parton
Randy Parton, born Dec. 15, 1953, died in 2021 at the age of 67. On Jan. 21, 2021, Dolly shared his death on Facebook, revealing that her brother had died from cancer.

“The family and I are grieving his loss, but we know he is in a better place than we are at this time,” the country icon said in her statement. “We are a family of faith, and we believe that he is with God and that he is joined by members of the family that have gone on before and have welcomed him with joy and open arms.”

Like his older sister, Randy Parton achieved success in music and entertainment. Famous for his headline performances at Dollywood, the singer-songwriter released several hits that graced Billboard’s Hot Country Songs chart, including “Hold Me Like You Never Had Me,” “Shot Full of Love,” “Don’t Cry Baby,” “Oh, No” and “A Stranger in Her Bed,” according to the music publication.
Larry Parton
Larry Parton, Robert and Avie Lee Parton’s ninth child and fifth son, died days after his birth in July 1955. Dolly Parton was 9 years old at the time of her brother’s death.
Floyd Parton
Floyd Parton and twin sister Freida Parton were born June 1, 1957. Like many of his siblings, Floyd Parton pursued a career in the music industry, often collaborating with Dolly Parton.
He penned her 1991 duet with Ricky Van Shelton, “Rockin’ Years” and wrote “Nickels and Dimes” for her 1978 album “Heartbreaker.”
Floyd Parton died Dec. 6, 2018, at the age of 61. The Parton family paid tribute to Floyd Parton at a private memorial in Tennessee, reported Billboard.

“Dolly, and the entire Parton family, wish to thank everyone for their kindness,” the family said in a statement to People at the time. “Yesterday, we laid our sweet baby brother to rest. We all sang his lovely song, ‘Rockin’ Years,’ together as a family at the service to say goodbye to him. He lived a short life of love and beautiful songs.”
Freida Parton
Freida Parton, born June 1, 1957, is Floyd Parton’s twin sister. Freida Parton ventured into the realm of music but diverged from her family’s country origins, singing hard rock songs.

Later in life, Freida Parton became an ordained minister. She told Knoxville News Sentinel in an interview in April 2014 that she had opened Parton Family Wedding Chapel & Antiques, a wedding chapel and store, in the family’s native Sevierville, Tennessee. However, the business appears to have closed.
Rachel Parton George

Rachel Parton George was born on Aug. 31, 1959. She’s known for her portrayal of Doralee Rhodes Brooks in the ABC sitcom “9 to 5,” which was based on the 1980 comedy film of the same name that starred Dolly Parton.

In addition to acting, Rachel Parton George released a country album in 1984, per the Smoky Mountain DNA website. According to her author page for Penguin Random House, she also performed in her family’s singing group.
In September 2024, the youngest sibling of the Parton clan released a cookbook with sister Dolly Parton called “Good Lookin’ Cookin’: A Year of Meals.”
The wise-cracking relationship between the two was on display in a joint interview for InStyle in 2025 in which they answered fan mail while talking about their cookbook.
“What is one item everyone should have in their closet?” one fan asked.
“A little black dress,” Rachel said.
“Couple of skeletons,” Dolly said as Rachel broke out laughing.
Ahead of the release, Dolly Parton shared a picture of her and her sister on social media.

“The best part of creating this cookbook is getting to spend quality time with my sister Rachel,” Dolly Parton captioned the post with a red heart emoji. “We can’t wait to share our recipes with you all, pre-order now at the link in my bio!”
Coy and Robert Lee Parton Jr.
Dolly’s other siblings — her older brother Coy Parton and younger brother Robert Lee Parton Jr. — largely led lives out of the spotlight.
Coy Parton, who worked as a crane operator, died in July 2026, according to an obituary shared by Atchley Funeral Home. A cause of death was not provided.

title: Harry Styles Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton During Opening Night of MSG Concert Run
summary: Harry Styles honored Dolly Parton during the first night of his 30-concert residency on his “Together Together” tour at New York City’s Madison Square Garden.
story: Harry Styles honored Dolly Parton during the first night of his 30-concert residency on his “Together Together” tour at New York City’s Madison Square Garden on Aug. 26.
The “Watermelon Sugar” singer took a moment to pay tribute to the country music legend, who leaves behind an extraordinary legacy after her death this week at age 80.
“I just want to say a proper thank you to all the musicians over the years who have inspired me. Dolly, we love you. Thank you so much,” he said, as those in attendance roared, according to Variety.

Parton’s song “I Will Always Love You” then played over the sound system while many in the crowd held up lights from their phones to join in the tribute. Styles — who did not appear to sing, but encouraged others to join in — stood on the stage while Parton’s vocals played.

Parton died Aug. 25 after a brief period with cancer, her representatives said. A country music icon who also enjoyed many visits to TODAY, the “Jolene” singer’s death has been mourned by many in the music world and beyond.

“A world without Dolly doesn’t feel possible, real, or right,” Taylor Swift wrote in a statement. “But because of the eternally generous way she spent her time on this earth and the countless lives she changed for the better, her legacy will be an everlasting one.”
Eminem shared a letter Parton once wrote to him after they were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022, in which she complimented his work as a rapper.

“I’m sorry we never got a chance to meet, but getting this note from Dolly really had a an impact on me,” he wrote on Instagram. “She definitely didn’t have to take the time to do it. Even for a kid who mostly listened to rap music, she was an icon. A superstar in every sense. Rest easy Dolly. And thank you for the kind words.
Parton’s goddaughter, Miley Cyrus, also opened up about her death.
“The feeling of losing my Aunt Dolly is beyond what feels right to share,” she wrote Aug. 26 on Instagram, alongside a black and white photo of Parton.
“Our most sacred moments were private and they’ll stay there behind the stage, beneath the glamour & between our hearts,” she continued.

“What I KNOW is Dolly would want me to feel it, write a song about it, and then continue on and be strong. I have an angel by my side. I always have. One of our last conversations was about music and metamorphosis.

“🦋I will always love her and want to make her proud. My heart breaks for the world, her family and friends who will miss her deeply. We’re in this loss together and we will see her in all of the most beautiful things.”

title: I Teach a College Class on Dolly Parton. What We Can All Learn From Her
summary: A college professor explains why her class on Dolly Parton has lessons for everyone.
story: “Take It From Me” is a TODAY.com series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this latest installment, an anthropology professor explains what Dolly Parton has to teach us all.
The news of the Dolly Parton’s passing at the age of 80 led to an outpouring of tributes from peers in the industry and fans.
After hearing the news, anthropology professor Sarah Phillips spent part of the afternoon of “curled in a ball” in her office, “just outright mourning Dolly and all that we’ve lost.”
“It’s been a real roller coaster. Like many people, I think I never really believed she was mortal,” she tells TODAY.com.
For Phillips, Parton’s death felt personal. A professor of anthropology at Indiana University Bloomington, Phillips taught a course called “The Anthropology of Dolly Parton” for two years in a row.
“We have graduated around 120 ‘Dolliologists,’” Phillips says.

The course, which is taught every spring semester with the help of four undergraduate teaching assistants and a graduate associate instructor, uses Parton as a lens to study sociocultural anthropology.

Phillips says Parton’s story is one-of-a-kind, in that by following its arc, a person can learn about regional differences in America, class, fame, femininity, workers’ rights, women’s rights, queer culture, education and more.
“I can’t think of anyone else that this approach would work as seamlessly as it does,” Phillips says.

By now, Parton’s rise is the stuff of legend. Born the fourth of 12 siblings in a one-room cabin in Tennessee, Parton exhibited a love of music at an early age. By 13, Johnny Cash had introduced her at the Grand Ole Opry. She moved to Nashville after graduation. Her big break came in 1964, when she was hand-picked by Porter Wagoner to co-star on his syndicated TV show. Her decision to go solo and leave the show inspired the song “I Will Always Love You,” one of her biggest hits.

She was known as much for her song-writing prowess as her distinct appearance, entrepreneurship and philanthropy. She was also a devoted wife, aunt and godmother. Parton was beloved in her home state for many reasons, including investing in the local economy by building Dollywood in Pigeon Forge.
The class uses Parton’s story as a way to talk about, well, America.

“We talk about regional stereotypes. We talk about language and dialect. We talk about the history of different forms of music, especially country music, and how it moved from different parts of Europe through the United States down to the South, and how Dolly and her people were part of that movement.”

At one point in the semester, the class watches “9 to 5,” the 1980 film Parton starred in with Lily Tomlin and Jane Fonda and wrote the lead song for, and connects it to the real-life office workers’ movement originating in Boston.
Another class is a lesson on regional stereotypes in the U.S, like how the idea of the hillbilly and redneck are curated and challenged in Parton’s album art and different periods of her career.

She also tries to impart Parton’s message, which she summarizes like this: “If you have a dream and you put in the work, because she sure did work, you can do anything that you want to. Despite the hurdles that are going to be put up in front of you by naysayers, by people who want to see you fail, by people who think they have your best interests at heart but are giving you advice — listen to your heart.”
What also fascinates Phillips is Parton’s undeniably wide appeal, and what caused it.

“She was so genuine beneath the big hair, beneath the rhinestones, the acrylic nails, the over-the-top look that she curated. As she would say, ‘Where it counts, I’m real.’ And she really connected with people on a personal level,” Phillips said. “Dolly Parton often said, ‘When people come to see me, they’re really coming to see themselves,’ and so she knew that people looked to her as a reflection of all that was good in themselves, and she really leaned into that.”
Phillips says the students leave the class inspired by Parton’s story. Many have reached out in the wake of her death, hoping to gather.

“They want to go out and change the world, and they want to do so in a way that is caring and kind and energetic and in line with their moral compass, and they see how Dolly did that, and it really inspires them,” she says.
While not everyone can take “The Anthropology of Dolly,” Phillips provided us with a mini curriculum. She says the course was inspired by the nine-episode podcast “Dolly Parton’s America.”

“Start with ‘Dolly Parton’s America,’ there is a treasure trove. There’s so many wonderful people interviewed in that podcast, so many different perspectives presented,” Phillips says. “Then, go after those authors, see what they’ve written.”
There’s another thing Phillips says we do: “Keep her memory alive.”

“I have no doubt that that’s going to happen, but we also have to think through these questions that you’re asking me,” Phillips explains. “What made her so special? What made her this uniting figure? Something that you know the one person all Americans can agree on, and can we all try to cultivate that just a little bit in ourselves? It would be a much better world if we could.”

title: Tim Curry Honored By ‘Rocky Horror Picture Show’ Co-Stars
summary: Tim Curry’s “The Rocky Horror Picture Show” co-stars are sharing their memories of filming the cult classic with the actor following the news of his death.
story: Tim Curry’s “The Rocky Horror Picture Show” co-stars are sharing their memories of filming the cult classic with the actor following the news of his death.

Curry, who delivered an unforgettable performance of Dr. Frank-N-Furter in the musical, died peacefully at his home in Toluca Lake, Los Angeles, on Aug. 25, his representatives confirmed in a statement to NBC News. His longtime manager and friend Marcia Hurwitz shared the news of his passing, as well. Curry was 80 years old.

The English actor, also known for his roles in “Clue” and the 1990 TV version of “It,” was honored by the many actors he shared the screen with. Members of “The Rocky Horror Picture Show” cast, including Susan Sarandon, posted sweet tributes to Curry.
Read on to see what they said about working with Curry and how they will remember him.
Susan Sarandon
Sarandon, who portrayed Janet Weiss in the 1975 film, uploaded a slideshow of photos of Curry to Instagram. The final picture showed Curry dressed in his Dr. Frank-N-Furter costume.
“What a funny, sexy, original he was. But what I loved about him most was his heart,” Sarandon said about her former co-star.

“Even wheelchair bound he continued to be so sweet and generous with his fans,” she added, referring to the stroke Curry suffered in 2012 that impacted his mobility. “Thank you Tim for meaning so much to so many people. Love you, S.”
Barry Bostwick
Barry Bostwick, who portrayed Janet’s fiancé Brad Majors, referenced lines from “The Rocky Horror Picture Show” in his Facebook tribute.
“The river was deep but you swam it. The road was long but you ran it” Dammit Tim, I love you…” he wrote, a play on lyrics from the song “Dammit Janet.”
Luke Evans

Luke Evans, who took on the role of Dr. Frank-N-Furter for the Broadway production of the musical and earned a nomination at the 79th Tony Awards, shared a letter on Instagram that he wrote to Curry three weeks before his death.

“I want to share it with you, he was a force, a bright fierce flame, an exquisite charm and that rich vocal tone, he was an inspiration to me and so many more people for the roles he played and the effect he had on so many of us. There will only be one Tim Curry. And the rest of us will just have to do our best to emulate some of the magic of that role that I’ve just spent 7 months playing…,” he said before including the message.
In the letter, Evans said although they had never met he felt Curry’s presence since he started working on the production.
“Being compared to you has been one of the greatest compliments I’ve ever received, even though it’s a comparison no one could ever hope to live up to,” he said, in part.
Evans added, “I’ve never tried to recreate what you did. That would be impossible. I simply hoped to honour the extraordinary character you brought to life, while finding my own way through him.”
‘The Rocky Horror Picture Show’
The Instagram account for “The Rocky Horror Picture Show,” which was co-written by fellow cast member Richard O’Brien, described Curry as a “singular talent.”

“A true original. And the man who first brought Dr. Frank-N-Furter to life,” the post said. “When The Rocky Horror Show began in 1973, nobody could have imagined what would follow. But from the moment Tim stepped onto that stage, something extraordinary happened. He didn’t simply play a character. He created an icon.”
The post continued, “Thank you, Tim. For the brilliance. For the courage. For the inspiration. For Frank. And for everything that followed. You were, and always will be, unforgettable.”

title: Dolly Parton Had Many Projects In the Works Before Her Death. Where They Stand
summary: Dolly Parton’s team shares an update on all the projects she was working on and would be releasing.
story: Before her death, Dolly Parton had a slew of projects she was excited about bringing to life and sharing with her millions of fans.
On Aug. 26, a day after the country icon died at the age of 80, her team shared an update on all the plans she had in development.

“Dolly worked up until the day she died. She loved seeing her dreams come to life, and loved knowing her work brought people joy,” her longtime manager Danny Nozell said in a press release. “Ever the planner, Dolly worked with the team that she handpicked, for the past several years to build a project roadmap that will guide us for decades to come.”
Parton died after being diagnosed with cancer, her estate announced Aug. 25 in a statement. She had not publicly disclosed her diagnosis, but had been open about her ongoing health challenges.

While the beloved star’s death came as a shock to many, she prepared for her legacy to live on. Nozell said in his statement that he and Parton’s team will oversee the many projects she had been working on and “ensure the many dreams she had yet to fulfill are brought to life.”
He noted that many projects were in various stages of development, stressing that Parton approved everything that would be shared on her official channels.

“If you see unreleased music, products, books, experiences, and campaigns launched through official Dolly Parton channels, you can have confidence in knowing that she placed her personal stamp on it.”
The “9 to 5” singer’s team also shared a video compilation of Parton hard at work, promoting some upcoming content.

Parton’s team also said that details on additional projects, including an avatar show she previously spoke about, a biopic, docuseries, scripted series, a Billy The Kid animated series and many more “will be revealed soon.”
Below, an overview of the active Parton projects and some of their release dates.
